speaker_role: current admissions officers (Assumption University, Drew University, George Washington University, Trinity University)
commercial_incentive: Coalition for College promotes its shared application platform (Scoir); panelists' own schools are being represented, but content is a public-service fact-or-fiction webinar rather than paid consulting
key_insights: Applying early (EA/ED) doesn't strongly increase odds at most schools overall, but can matter for limited-seat programs (nursing, engineering) and some scholarships; ED is a signed binding contract, not something a student can trigger accidentally

Standardized tests are treated as one 'complementary' piece of a holistic file rather than the dominant factor; GW has been test-optional since 2015 and reviews scores alongside, not above, other materials
Long, 'impressive-sounding' extracurricular lists matter less than depth and explaining time spent on work or family responsibilities, which admissions offices say they do want to see
Course rigor is evaluated relative to what a student's own high school offers, not against an absolute AP/IB course count
Prestige and acceptance rate are described as poor indicators of overall student success or fit; panel cites students commonly having multiple good options
Merit scholarships and outside awards are frequently missed because students research or apply for them too late; panelists recommend tracking eligible awards well before senior year
specific_numbers_or_facts: GW has been test-optional since 2015 (per Federico Glitman, GW)
National college acceptance rate cited as roughly 72% for that year (per Federico Glitman)
Cited that 87% of students change their major during their first year of college (per Federico Glitman)
Most selective institutions' acceptance rates cited as roughly 2-4% (per Ellen Johnson, Drew)
notable_or_distinctive: Real-time 'fact or fiction' panel of four current admissions officers from different institution types directly rebutting common myths, including a specific anecdote about a student's birdwatching interest becoming a memorable interview topic.
reliability_notes: Panelists speak to their own institutions' practices, which may not generalize broadly; several numeric claims (72% acceptance rate, 87% major-change rate) are stated without citation; minor auto-caption artifacts throughout.
